Recursion is a programming technique where a function calls itself to solve a smaller piece of the same problem. Each recursive call works on a reduced input, and the process repeats until it reaches a simple case that can be solved directly—this is called the base case. Once the base case is reached, the function returns its result, and each previous call “unwinds,” passing its own result back up the chain. By breaking a complex task into identical, smaller subtasks, recursion lets you express elegant solutions that would be cumbersome with only iterative loops.
